code.title: Matrix Reader and Printer
code.description:
A teacher types a class marks grid into a grading tool. Read the number of rows R and columns C, then R*C integers that fill the matrix row by row. Print the matrix exactly as given, one row per line with values separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order (all of row 1, then row 2, and so on).

Output Format:
R lines, each containing the C integers of that row separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Matrix Row Sum Reporter
code.description:
A fitness coach logs the reps each athlete completes on several stations in a grid. Read R and C, then the R*C log values in row-major order. Print the matrix, then a summary line with the sum of every row.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines with the matrix rows (values separated by single spaces), then one line:
Row sums: <sum of row 1> <sum of row 2> ... <sum of row R>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, 0 <= element <= 100

code.title: Matrix Column Sum Reporter
code.description:
A canteen manager tracks how many plates of each dish were sold at every counter, stored as a grid. Read R and C, then the R*C sales values in row-major order. Print the matrix, then a summary line with the sum of every column.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines with the matrix rows (values separated by single spaces), then one line:
Column sums: <sum of column 1> <sum of column 2> ... <sum of column C>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, 0 <= element <= 100

code.title: Largest Element Locator
code.description:
A quality team scans a defect score grid and must know where the worst defect is. Read R and C, then the R*C scores in row-major order. Print the largest score and its position (1-based row and column). If the largest value appears several times, report the first occurrence when scanning rows from top to bottom and each row left to right.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
Largest: <value>
Row: <row number, 1-based>
Column: <column number, 1-based>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Matrix Total Sum
code.description:
A battery pack arranges its cells in a grid and the controller reports the total capacity. Read R and C, then the R*C cell values in row-major order, and print the sum of every element.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
Total sum: <sum of all R*C elements>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Zero Cell Counter
code.description:
A sensor grid reports 0 when a sensor is offline and any other value when it is active. Read R and C, then the R*C readings in row-major order, and count how many cells are exactly 0.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
Zero count: <number of cells equal to 0>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Seat Booking Map
code.description:
An auditorium seats visitors in a grid; each cell is 0 for available or 1 for booked. Read R and C, then the R*C seat states in row-major order. Print the seat map where every 0 becomes 'A' (available) and every 1 becomes 'B' (booked), one row per line with no spaces, then print how many seats are booked.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C values, each 0 or 1, in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines of A/B characters (C characters per line, no spaces), then:
Booked: <number of 1s>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, each value is 0 or 1
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= R, C <= 50, each value is 0 or 1

code.title: Temperature Grid Report
code.description:
A weather bureau arranges its stations in a grid and needs the peak reading of every belt (row). Read R and C, then the R*C readings in row-major order, then print the maximum reading of each row.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines, one per row:
Row <i> max: <largest value in row i>
(rows are numbered from 1)

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -50 <= element <= 60
code.output1:
Row 1 max: 20
Row 2 max: 30
Row 3 max: 15

code.title: Pixel Brightness Grid
code.description:
A phone camera reduces an image to a tiny grid of brightness values from 0 to 255. Read R and C, then the R*C pixel values in row-major order, and print the average brightness with exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
Average brightness: <average of all pixels with exactly 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, 0 <= element <= 255

code.title: Warehouse Rack Loads
code.description:
A warehouse has R racks and every rack holds C shelves; each shelf stores one weight in kg. Read R and C, then the R*C weights in row-major order. Print the total load of every rack and name the heaviest rack; if several racks tie, pick the one with the smallest rack number.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines, one per rack:
Rack <i> load: <sum of row i>
Then:
Heaviest rack: <rack number> (load <that load>)

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, 0 <= element <= 500
code.sampleoutput1:
Rack 1 load: 60
Rack 2 load: 15
Heaviest rack: 1 (load 60)
code.output1:
Rack 1 load: 3
Rack 2 load: 18
Rack 3 load: 6
Heaviest rack: 2 (load 18)
code.output2:
Rack 1 load: 5
Rack 2 load: 5
Heaviest rack: 1 (load 5)
code.output3:
Rack 1 load: 0
Rack 2 load: 0
Heaviest rack: 1 (load 0)

code.title: Section Score Merger
code.description:
Two sections of a course wrote the same test and the coordinator stores both score grids with the same shape. Read R and C, then the R*C scores of section A, then the R*C scores of section B. Print the combined grid obtained by adding the two matrices cell by cell.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers (matrix A) in row-major order.
Then: R*C integers (matrix B) in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines with the sum matrix, values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -100 <= element <= 100

code.title: Warehouse Stock Comparison
code.description:
A warehouse chain compares stock counts of the same products in two depots. Read R and C, then depot 1 counts, then depot 2 counts (same shape). Print the difference matrix depot1 - depot2 cell by cell; a negative value means depot 2 holds more of that product.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers (depot 1) in row-major order.
Then: R*C integers (depot 2) in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines with the difference matrix (depot1 - depot2), values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -100 <= element <= 100

code.title: Seating Chart Flip
code.description:
An event coordinator stores a seating chart as a grid and the display software needs it flipped: rows must become columns. Read R and C, then the R*C chart values in row-major order, and print the transpose of the matrix.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
C lines; line j contains the values of column j of the original matrix separated by single spaces (the transpose has C rows and R columns).

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -100 <= element <= 100

code.title: Game Board Diagonal Scan
code.description:
A treasure board game uses a square grid; the two diagonal paths score separately. Read the board size (R and C on the first line, both equal to N), then the N*N board values in row-major order. Print the sum of the main diagonal (top-left to bottom-right) and the sum of the anti-diagonal (top-right to bottom-left).

Input Format:
First line: R and C with R = C = N.
Then: N*N integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
Main diagonal sum: <sum of a[i][i]>
Anti-diagonal sum: <sum of a[i][N-1-i]>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 50, -100 <= element <= 100, R = C guaranteed

code.title: Festival Light Fence Survey
code.description:
A festival ground is decorated with lights on a grid; only the border cells (first and last row, first and last column) glow. Read R and C, then the R*C light values in row-major order, and print the sum of all border cells. A single-row or single-column grid has every cell on the border, and each cell is counted only once.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
Border sum: <sum of all perimeter cells>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, 0 <= element <= 100

code.title: Poster Brightness Scaler
code.description:
A design tool scales every level of a poster grid by a whole-number factor. Read R and C, then the R*C levels in row-major order, then the multiplier k on the last line. Print the scaled grid (every element multiplied by k).

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.
Last line: the integer multiplier k.

Output Format:
R lines with the scaled matrix, values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, 0 <= element <= 1000, 0 <= k <= 10

code.title: Assembly Line Grid Multiplier
code.description:
An assembly plant tracks items moving through stages; the stage-count grid (R1 x C1) is multiplied by the routing-weight grid (R2 x C2) to compute line totals. The two matrices are always compatible for multiplication (C1 = R2 guaranteed). Read the dimensions and both grids, echo the dimensions, then print the product matrix.

Input Format:
First line: R1 and C1.
Second line: R2 and C2 (C1 = R2 guaranteed).
Then: R1*C1 integers (matrix A) in row-major order.
Then: R2*C2 integers (matrix B) in row-major order.

Output Format:
A size: <R1>x<C1>
B size: <R2>x<C2>
Result size: <R1>x<C2>
Then R1 lines with the product matrix, values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R1, C1, R2, C2 <= 50, C1 = R2, -1000 <= element <= 1000
code.sampleoutput1:
A size: 2x2
B size: 2x2
Result size: 2x2
19 22
43 50
code.sampleoutput2:
A size: 1x2
B size: 2x1
Result size: 1x1
11
code.output1:
A size: 2x3
B size: 3x2
Result size: 2x2
58 64
139 154
code.output2:
A size: 1x1
B size: 1x1
Result size: 1x1
35
code.output3:
A size: 2x2
B size: 2x3
Result size: 2x3
9 8 7
6 5 4

code.title: Signboard Spiral Scan
code.description:
A stadium signboard stores a grid of numbers and the controller scans them in spiral order: start at the top-left corner, move right across the top row, then down the rightmost column, then left across the bottom row, then up the leftmost column, and repeat inward until every cell has been visited. Read R and C, then the R*C values in row-major order, and print the spiral scan.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
R*C lines, one visited element per line in spiral order.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -1000 <= element <= 1000

code.title: Exam Hall Heatmap Analyzer
code.description:
An exam hall monitoring system stores an activity level (0 to 100) for every seat and produces a row-by-row heatmap report. Read R and C, then the R*C levels in row-major order. Print the average level of every row with exactly two decimals, then the row with the highest average; if several rows tie, report the smallest row number.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines:
Row <i> average: <average of row i, 2 decimals>
Then:
Highest average row: <row number> (<its average, 2 decimals>)

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, 0 <= element <= 100
code.sampleoutput1:
Row 1 average: 20.00
Row 2 average: 5.00
Highest average row: 1 (20.00)
code.output1:
Row 1 average: 50.00
Row 2 average: 65.00
Row 3 average: 0.00
Highest average row: 2 (65.00)
code.output2:
Row 1 average: 1.50
Row 2 average: 3.50
Highest average row: 2 (3.50)
code.output3:
Row 1 average: 5.00
Row 2 average: 5.00
Highest average row: 1 (5.00)
code.whitelist: for, if, cin, cout, fixed, setprecision

code.title: Radar Signal Cluster Scanner
code.description:
A harbour radar paints a grid where 1 marks a radar echo and 0 marks clear water. Operators count signals in two passes: along each row, a group is a maximal run of consecutive 1s; the same rule applies vertically along each column. Read R and C, then the R*C echoes in row-major order, and print the total number of row groups and column groups.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C values, each 0 or 1, in row-major order.

Output Format:
Row groups: <total horizontal runs of consecutive 1s over all rows>
Column groups: <total vertical runs of consecutive 1s over all columns>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, each value is 0 or 1
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= R, C <= 50, each value is 0 or 1
